                    ### Question
                    A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician for gradual worsening of her vision. Her father died at 40 years of age. She is 181 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 69 kg (152 lb); BMI is 21 kg/m2. A standard vision test shows severe myopia. Genetic analysis shows an FBN1 gene mutation on chromosome 15. This patient is at greatest risk of mortality due to which of the following causes?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Obstruction of the superior vena cava lumen
opb. Increased pressure in the pulmonary arteries
opc. Eccentric ventricular hypertrophy
opd. Supraventricular tachyarrhythmia
ope. Intimal tear of the aortic root

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The FBN1 gene mutation is associated with Marfan syndrome, a connective tissue disorder that significantly increases the risk of cardiovascular complications, particularly involving the aorta. This includes aortic dilation, which can lead to aortic dissection and intimal tears of the aortic root. The reasoning chains correctly identify the risk of an intimal tear of the aortic root as a major cause of mortality in this patient. Other options, such as obstruction of the superior vena cava, increased pressure in the pulmonary arteries, eccentric ventricular hypertrophy, and supraventricular tachyarrhythmia, are less directly related to the primary risks associated with Marfan syndrome. Therefore, the most significant risk of mortality for this patient is indeed an intimal tear of the aortic root.
